entities.name: Elisha Reynolds Potter
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Elisha Reynolds Potter (1764–1835) was an American Federalist and later Democratic-Republican politician from Rhode Island who served in the U.S. House (1796–1797 and 1809–1815). A Rhode Island congressman serving across two distinct eras — the Washington Federalist period and the Madison War of 1812 era — Potter's combined service illustrated the partisan transformation of New England from Federalist to Jeffersonian Democratic-Republican allegiance. Rhode Island's resistance to the War of 1812 — the war was widely unpopular in New England's commercially-minded, anti-French maritime communities — was a defining feature of Potter's second House period.

New England's Hartford Convention (1814–1815) — the gathering of Federalist New England states protesting the war — was the climax of the regional political crisis during Potter's service.

His son Elisha Reynolds Potter Jr. would serve in Congress in the next generation.

He was a South Kingstown Rhode Island planter-lawyer.
